To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
serum glutathione (an antioxidant) and malondaldehyde (an oxidant) levels are decreased and increased, respectively, in patients with late pulmonary complications of sulfur mustard intoxication.
the serum levels of MDA and glutathione in patients with sulfur mustards induced lung injury were higher and lower than those in controls, respectively.

the mean GSH level was significantly lower and the MDA level was significantly higher in patients with SM-induced lung injuries compared with healthy nonsmoking controls, and the severity of the pulmonary injury did not affect the level of MDA but did affect the level of GSH.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the oxidative-antoxidative system and its role in the development and progression of late pulmonary complications of SM gas intoxication.
the oxidative-antioxida-tive balance in patients suffering from late SM-induced lung injuries.
the antioxidant and oxidant status of patients with SM-induced lung injuries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the oxidative-antioxident status of the lung tissue is not related to the severity or extent of pulmonary dysfunction in patients with SM-induced lung injury.
oxidative stress is not a major factor in the development and progression of SM-induced lung injuries.
the oxidative-antioxative system is altered and this is a factor in the development of late pulmonary complications of SM intoxication.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the antioxidant and oxidative stress parameters are related to the severity and the degree of pulmonary impairment in patients with late SM-induced lung injuries.
the serum GSH and the MDA level could be used to evaluate the severity of SM-induced lung injuries and also to follow the course of treatment.
the antioxidant capacity is decreased and the oxidant capacity is increased in SM-intoxicated patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the antioxidant system is involved in the pathogenesis of SM-induced lung injuries and that the oxidative-antoxidant system may be a useful biomarker for assessing the severity of SM-induced lung injury.
the serum level of GHS and MDA is an indicator of the severity of lung injuries in patients exposed to SM.
oxidative stress plays an important role in the pathophysiology of SM-induced lung injuries.
